message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points (Texas) | Where to Find the Law | |-------|--------------------|-----------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type:
• 55 mph on rural interstates,
• 45 mph on urban interstates,
• 35–40 mph on most state highways,
• 25–30 mph in residential zones.
• “No Speed Limit” signs allow up to 75 mph on some rural roads. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All drivers and front‑seat passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must use a child safety seat or booster.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children under 13. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.002–545.004 | | **DUI / Driving Under Influence** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal for all drivers.
• Lower BAC limits apply to commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, jail time, and mandatory alcohol‑education programs. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.021–545.023 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Violations carry a fine of $50–$100. | Texas Transportation Code §545.025 | | **Headlights & Signal Use** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, after dark, or when visibility is reduced.
• Turn signals must be used at least 100 ft before turning or changing lanes. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.030–545.032 | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Stop at stop signs; yield at yield signs.
• At uncontrolled intersections, give right‑of‑way to vehicles approaching from the right.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.040–545.045 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children.
• Stopping distance: 20 ft for passenger cars, 30 ft for trucks. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.050–545.052 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Drivers must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle being overtaken is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.060–545.062 | | **Parking Regulations** | • Parking on sidewalks, crosswalks, or in front of fire hydrants is prohibited.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.070–545.072 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.080–545.082 | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Commercial vehicles must follow specific weight, size, and driver‑licensing requirements.
• Motorcycles require a motorcycle endorsement. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.090–545.092 | --- ### How to Get the Full Text of the Laws 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic regulations. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.545.htm 2. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Provides driver’s handbook, licensing information, and enforcement updates. *Website:* https://www.dps.texas.gov/ 3. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Offers road‑condition reports, construction notices, and public‑transportation guidelines. *Website:* https://www.txdot.gov/ 4. **Texas Legislature Online** – For legislative history, amendments, and bill tracking. *Website:* https://capitol.texas.gov/ --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – hands‑free only. - **Observe posted speed limits** – they’re designed for safety. - **Check for school buses** – stop even if you’re not in the same lane. - **Use turn signals early** – helps prevent collisions. - **Stay alert for pedestrians** – especially in residential areas. --- #### Need More Specific Information? If you’re looking for details on a particular aspect (e.g., “What are the penalties for texting while driving?” or “How does Texas handle DUI for commercial drivers?”), let me know and I can pull up the exact statute or provide additional resources.
